examples: *If you charge your phone*, it will work all day. (if + present simple)
I *will download* the app if the wifi is fast. (will shows the result)
She *will not* open the app *unless* she knows the password. (unless = if not)
I will call you *as soon as* I finish the download. (as soon as + present simple)
We *will* start the movie *when* the screen is ready. (when + present simple)
grammar.explanation:
Use the **first conditional** to talk about a real result in the future.

The rule is simple: **if + present simple**, then **will + verb**.

**Will** shows the result. It always goes in the second part.

Never put **will** after **if**. Say **if you charge your phone**, not if you will charge your phone.

**Unless** means **if not**. It is a short way to say the same idea.

After **when**, **as soon as**, **until**, **before**, and **after**, use the **present simple** for the future. Never use **will** there.
